method: Checked on the dates shown using web search extracts. The session that built this register could not open ontario.ca or canada.ca directly (network policy), so no claim is marked PRIMARY_TEXT_READ. Upgrade a claim only after reading the cited provision on the official page.

claims.claim: An ONCA corporation must have at least three directors. The articles may set a minimum and maximum number.

sources.title: Bill 65, Not-for-Profit Corporations Act, 2010 (explanatory note), Legislative Assembly of Ontario
Not-for-Profit Corporations Act, 2010, S.O. 2010, c. 15 (e-Laws)

claims.claim: Every director must be an individual, at least 18 years old, not bankrupt, and not found incapable of managing property. A director does not have to live in Ontario or in Canada.

sources.title: CLEO Nonprofit Law Ontario: who can be a director
Carters, Board of Directors Issues and Meetings under the ONCA (2021)

claims.note: The original kit said a majority of directors must be individuals. That is wrong: a corporation or other entity cannot be a director at all.

claims.claim: A person becomes a director only with their consent. Keep each director's signed consent in the minute book.

sources.title: CLEO Nonprofit Law Ontario: who can be a director

claims.claim: ONCA does not use the terms soliciting and non-soliciting; those belong to the federal Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act. The ONCA category is the public benefit corporation: a charitable corporation, or a non-charitable corporation that receives more than $10,000 in a financial year in donations or gifts from people who are not its members, directors, officers or employees, or in government grants or similar assistance. The status applies from the following financial year.

sources.title: Miller Thomson, ONCA Fast Facts: Public Benefit Corporations
Charity Law Group, What is a Public Benefit Corporation under ONCA?

claims.note: The original kit's soliciting versus non-soliciting choice does not exist in Ontario. The Institute does not choose this status; its funding sources decide it each year.

claims.claim: A public benefit corporation is limited in how many of its directors may be employees of the corporation or its affiliates. The limit is believed to be one-third.

sources.title: Ontario Nonprofit Network, Board Essentials (2021)

claims.note: The source confirms a restriction exists. The one-third figure was not confirmed.
claims.action: Read ONCA s. 23(3) on e-Laws before any director is put on payroll.

claims.claim: Members appoint an auditor each year unless they waive it. Public benefit corporation: annual revenue of $100,000 or less may waive both audit and review engagement; more than $100,000 and less than $500,000 may substitute a review engagement; $500,000 or more requires an audit. Other corporations: $500,000 or less may waive both; more than $500,000 may substitute a review engagement. Each waiver needs an extraordinary resolution and lasts only until the next annual meeting.

sources.title: Charity Law Group, Can not-for-profit corporations waive audit and review engagements under ONCA?
Ontario, Rules for not-for-profit and charitable corporations

claims.note: The dollar thresholds can be changed by regulation. Recheck them each year before the annual meeting.

claims.claim: Incorporation is by Articles of Incorporation under ONCA (Form 5270), filed through the Ontario Business Registry or by mail. The government fee is $155.
claims.authority: ONCA ss. 7 to 9; Ministry fee schedule

sources.title: Ontario, Guide to the Not-for-Profit Corporations Act, 2010
LawyerInfo, How to incorporate a not-for-profit corporation under the ONCA in Ontario

claims.note: The fee comes from private guides, not the official schedule. Processing time is not settled: sources give five business days, seven business days, and two to three weeks. One outlier gives a $350 fee. Confirm the fee on the registry's payment screen.

claims.claim: A named corporation needs an Ontario-biased NUANS name search report dated not more than 90 days before the articles are filed. A Canada-biased report is not accepted. The Ministry does not run the search; a private search house does.

sources.title: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, notice for not-for-profit incorporation (ON00206E)
Form 5270E, Articles of Incorporation (ONCA)

claims.claim: The words college, institute and university (and their French forms) are restricted in an ONCA corporate name where the word would suggest the corporation is a university, a college of applied arts and technology, or another post-secondary educational institution. Using the word then needs written consent from the Minister of Colleges and Universities.

sources.title: O. Reg. 394/21: Names and Filings (e-Laws)

claims.note: One extract of this wording was labelled as not yet in force, so the exact current text is not settled. The risk is real either way: the proposed name contains Institute and the proposed purposes are educational.

claims.claim: A proposed name that is the same as, or likely to be confused with, an existing corporation's name can be refused. Written consent from the existing corporation may be required.

sources.title: O. Reg. 394/21: Names and Filings (e-Laws)

claims.note: The secondary sources found describe the predecessor Act. If ClearGlass Inc. is on the register, the NUANS report will list it.
claims.action: Ask the search house or filing agent whether a consent from ClearGlass Inc. is needed, and get it in writing before filing if so.

claims.claim: An ONCA corporation may instead take a number name: its corporation number followed by Ontario Non-Profit and an approved word or abbreviation. A number name needs no NUANS report.

sources.title: O. Reg. 394/21: Names and Filings (e-Laws)

claims.note: The extract confirms the number-name format. That no NUANS report is needed for it follows from L-08 applying to named corporations and was not separately confirmed.

claims.claim: Every Ontario corporation, including a not-for-profit, must file an initial return within 60 days after the date of incorporation.

sources.title: Form 5284 and instructions: Initial Return / Notice of Change / Annual Return by an Ontario Corporation
Corporations Information Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.39 (e-Laws)

claims.note: The original kit left this filing out.

claims.claim: An Ontario not-for-profit corporation must file an annual return through the Ontario Business Registry within six months after the end of each financial year.

sources.title: Corporations Information Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.39 (e-Laws)
Charity Law Group, What are the required government filings for an Ontario nonprofit?

claims.claim: A notice of change must be filed within 15 days after a change of directors, officers or registered office.

sources.title: Charity Law Group, What are the required government filings for an Ontario nonprofit?

claims.note: Official extracts found state the 15-day period only for extra-provincial corporations.

claims.claim: The first annual meeting of members must be held not later than 18 months after incorporation, and each later one not later than 15 months after the one before.

sources.title: Carters, Membership Issues and Meetings under the ONCA (2021)

claims.claim: Whether ONCA also requires the annual meeting within six months after the financial year end is disputed between the sources found. Holding it within six months satisfies either reading, so the calendar uses that as the planning date.

sources.title: CLEO Nonprofit Law Ontario: annual general meetings
Carters, Membership Issues and Meetings under the ONCA (2021)

claims.note: CLEO states a six-month rule. Carters states ONCA has none. CLEO also says financial statements go to members before the meeting.
claims.action: Read ONCA ss. 52, 83 and 84 on e-Laws and record the rule here.

claims.claim: Directors may make, amend or repeal a by-law. It takes effect when the board passes it but only until the next meeting of members, where members confirm, reject or amend it by ordinary resolution. If members do not confirm it, it stops having effect.

sources.title: CLEO Nonprofit Law Ontario: how to change bylaws

claims.claim: If a corporation passes no organizational by-laws within 60 days after incorporation, it is deemed to have passed the Ministry's standard organizational by-laws.

sources.title: Carters, By-law Issues to Consider under the ONCA (2021)
Ontario, Not-for-Profit Corporations Act, 2010: standard organizational by-law

claims.claim: Where remaining property goes on dissolution depends on the type of corporation. A corporation that is not a public benefit corporation follows its articles, or failing that distributes to members. A charitable corporation must give its property to a Canadian body with similar purposes, the Crown or a municipality. The permitted recipients for a non-charitable public benefit corporation were not confirmed.

sources.title: Ministry notice on articles of dissolution under ONCA (ON00208E)
CLEO Nonprofit Law Ontario: dissolution

claims.note: The kit's dissolution clause names qualified donees under the Income Tax Act. That wording has to work under ONCA for each status the Institute may hold and under the CRA's requirements for a future charity.
claims.action: Have counsel settle the dissolution clause before the articles are filed. Articles are expensive to amend.

claims.claim: Only a registered charity or other qualified donee can issue official donation receipts. A non-profit organization cannot, even though it may be exempt from income tax.

sources.title: Canada Revenue Agency, charities media kit: questions and answers

claims.claim: An application for charitable registration is made online through the CRA's My Business Account. The paper Form T2050 named in the original kit is no longer the route.

sources.title: Canada Revenue Agency, Submit your application

claims.note: The online route is confirmed. The date the paper form was withdrawn was not confirmed.

claims.claim: No official CRA service standard for reviewing a charity application was found. Secondary sources give four to twelve months. The original kit's 6 to 18 months is unconfirmed.

sources.title: Canada Revenue Agency, Application review process

claims.action: Read the CRA application review page and record the stated timeline. Do not promise funders a date.

claims.claim: The income tax exemption for a non-profit organization applies only to an organization that, in the Minister's opinion, is not a charity. An organization set up with exclusively charitable purposes that is not registered may therefore fit neither category and be taxable.

sources.title: Income Tax Act, s. 149 (Justice Laws)

claims.note: Stated from general knowledge of the provision; the text was not opened in this session. The kit's purposes are written as charitable purposes while the plan is to stay unregistered for at least a year. That combination is the exposure.
claims.action: Get a written opinion from a charity lawyer or CPA on the Institute's tax status in the unregistered period before the articles are filed.

claims.claim: A non-profit organization files information return T1044 if its interest, dividends, rentals and royalties exceeded $10,000 in the period, or its total assets exceeded $200,000 at the end of the preceding period, or it had to file one before. Draft federal legislation released in January 2026 would widen reporting, including a short return for organizations with receipts over $10,000.
claims.authority: Income Tax Act s. 149(12); CRA guide T4117

sources.title: Miller Thomson, NPO reporting rules recalibrated (2026)
Carters, Department of Finance releases new legislative proposals for NPO reporting

claims.note: Sources disagree on when the proposed rules would start (2026 tax years or fiscal years beginning in 2027). Whether they have been enacted was not confirmed.

claims.claim: A corporation files a T2 corporation income tax return for every tax year, including a tax-exempt non-profit with no tax payable, within six months after the year end. A registered charity files a T3010 instead.
claims.authority: Income Tax Act s. 150(1)(a); CRA guide T4012
claims.note: Stated from general knowledge; not checked in this session.
claims.action: Confirm with the Institute's accountant when the first year end is chosen.

claims.claim: It was not confirmed whether a CRA business number is issued automatically when an Ontario not-for-profit is incorporated.
claims.authority: CRA and Ontario Business Registry practice
claims.action: Check the incorporation confirmation for a business number. If there is none, register through CRA Business Registration Online.

claims.claim: ONCA has been in force since October 19, 2021.

sources.title: Ontario, Guide to the Not-for-Profit Corporations Act, 2010
